pass_a_gloss: And even if not on account of himself, as wise and passionless, the bridegroom turns the betrothed away from every staining, yet at least on account of her, seeing her stain and the loathing, he will do all the things able to heal and to turn her back, as to a self-authoritative nature bringing words turning away from whoring. What kind of pollution then would you think comes to be worse to a soul somehow proclaiming another god and not confessing the truly one and only Lord? And I think at least that, just as the one glued to the prostitute is one body, so the one confessing someone, and most of all in time of torture and examination of the faith, is mixed up and unified to the one confessed; but the one denying, by the very denial, in the manner of a sword cutting through, from that one whom he denies, undergoes the division, being separated from that one whom he denied. For which reason pay attention whether perhaps as following and necessary, the being confessed to happen to the confessor and the being denied to the denier, there has been said the: whoever confesses in me in front of the humans, I too will confess in him in front of my Father in the heavens. And would say the Word-itself and the Truth-itself to both the one having confessed and the one having denied: by what measure you measure it will be measured back to you; you then who measured by measure of the confession toward me and filled the measure of the confession will take back a measure of the confession from me, shaken, squeezed, overflowing, which will be given into your lap; and you who measured by the measure of the denial and denied me, will take back the proportionate to the measure of the denial, a measure of the denial from me about you.
pass_b_english: Even if the bridegroom, being wise and free from passion, does not turn his betrothed away from every defilement for his own sake, yet for her sake, seeing her defilement and her abomination, he will do everything that can heal her and turn her back, applying to her, as to a nature with free will, words that turn her away from fornication. What defilement, then, could you conceive worse for a soul than that it should in any way proclaim another god, and not confess the one who is truly the one and only Lord?

I think that, just as “he who is joined to a harlot is one body” (1 Corinthians 6:16), so the one who confesses someone, especially in a time of torture and of testing of faith, is blended and made one with the one he confesses; but the one who denies, by the denial itself, which cuts him off like a sword from the one he denies, suffers division, separated from the one he has denied. So consider whether perhaps it is as a consequence and a necessity, that being confessed befalls the one who confesses and being denied the one who denies, that the saying is spoken: “Whoever confesses in me before men, I too will confess in him before my Father in heaven” (Matthew 10:32).

And the very Word and very Truth might say both to the one who has confessed and to the one who has denied: “With the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you” (Luke 6:38). You, then, who measured with the measure of confession towards me, and filled up the measure of confession, will receive a measure of confession from me, shaken, pressed down and running over, which will be given “into your bosom”; and you who measured with the measure of denial, and denied me, will receive, in proportion to the measure of your denial, a measure of my denial of you.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. X); the old English was a digest; the old entry under this id was attached to the wrong chapter and did not carry the union of confessor and confessed or the two measures.

Read κἂν, δι᾽ ἐκείνην, καὶ τὸν βδελυγμόν, μὴ ὁμολογούσῃ, ὁ κολλώμενος, ἓν σῶμά ἐστιν, ὁμολογουμένῳ, ὃς ἐάν, ἀνθρώπων, αὐτοαλήθεια, ἀρνησαμένῳ, ᾧ μέτρῳ, καὶ, σεσαλευμένον (OCR υδεσαλευμένον), ὑπερεκχυνόμενον, εἰς, ἀπ᾽ ἐμοῦ, ἀρνήσεως.

choices.issue: ποῖον ... χείρονα γίνεσθαι ψυχῇ, ὅπως ποτὲ ἄλλον ἀγορευούσῃ θεόν
choices.choice: PTA confirms the text without ἤ; the dative participles describe the soul, rendered “worse for a soul than that it should in any way proclaim another god”.
Kept Origen's order “shaken, pressed down and running over”.
